react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific ORA, and mummichog m/z-network analysis) converge on Tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in this dataset. In the RaMP analysis, KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' ranks first with an FDR of 9.58×10⁻¹⁵ and a fold-enrichment of 667, with six driver metabolites mapping to the pathway: L-tryptophan, indoleacetaldehyde, tryptamine, serotonin, melatonin, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. The same pathway appears in WikiPathways (WP:WP465, FDR 1.14×10⁻¹⁴) and Reactome (REACT:R-HSA-209931 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis', FDR 6.64×10⁻⁸). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-only ORA confirms KEGG:hsa00380 at p = 1.59×10⁻⁸ with the identical six-compound overlap. Mummichog's m/z-direct analysis yields MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as its top hit (p = 8.40×10⁻⁵) with 13 of 14 pathway compounds matched, demonstrating that the mass-network also resolves this pathway from the input masses. The two convergent biological arms are the kynurenine branch (L-tryptophan → indoleacetaldehyde → tryptamine → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid) and the serotonin/melatonin branch (L-tryptophan → serotonin → melatonin). Acrolein, doxycycline, milrinone, and cytidine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate did not map to any tryptophan pathway across any paradigm, suggesting they belong to off-target or secondary metabolic modules. The near-unity cluster sizes from InChIKey reconciliation confirm all 10 input compounds are structurally distinct, ruling out namespace artefacts. The biological story is a coordinated perturbation of tryptophan catabolism — a pathway central to neurochemistry (serotonin, melatonin), immunomodulation (kynurenine metabolites), and NAD⁺ biosynthesis (via 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid).
